units.source_text: 先生刚才躺在缘台上时，后背沾了些土，我用两只手帮他掸掉了。

en.t: When Sensei had been lying on the bench a moment before, some dirt had stuck to his back, so I brushed it off for him with both hands.
There is not any resin stuck to it, is there?

units.source_text: “这件羽织是新做的，要是给弄脏了，回去要被妻子责怪的。

en.t: This haori is newly made, and if I get it dirty, my wife will scold me when I go home.

units.source_text: 我们又返回到斜坡上的房子跟前。

en.t: We returned once more to the house on the slope.

units.source_text: 我们进来时没看见人，这时却见女主人和一位十五六岁的小姑娘，坐在檐廊上往线板上缠线呢。

en.t: When we had come in we had seen no one, but now the mistress of the house and a girl of about fifteen or sixteen were sitting on the veranda winding thread onto a spool.

units.source_text: 我们走到大鱼缸旁边时，问候了一声：“真是打扰你们了。”

en.t: As we passed beside the large goldfish bowl, we said politely, Thank you for letting us trouble you.
Not at all, I am sorry we could not do more for you.

units.source_text: 女主人回礼后，又为刚才给小孩钱的事道了谢。

en.t: After returning the greeting, the mistress thanked us again for the money given to the child earlier.

units.source_text: 出了门，走过两三条街后，我终于忍不住对先生说：

en.t: After we left the gate and had walked two or three blocks, I finally could not hold back and said to Sensei:

units.source_text: “刚才先生说，任何人在关键时候都会变成坏人的。

en.t: You said earlier that anyone becomes a bad person at the crucial moment.
What did you mean by that?

units.source_text: “也没有很深的意思，这是事实，不是什么道理。”

en.t: There is no very deep meaning to it; it is a fact, not a theory.

units.source_text: “是不是事实没有关系，我想问的是，您所谓的关键的时候，到底是指什么场合。”

en.t: Whether it is a fact or not is beside the point; what I want to ask is what sort of situation you mean by the crucial moment.

units.source_text: 先生笑了起来，意思好像是说，已经没有谈论这个话题的兴致了，你问的不是时候。

en.t: Sensei began to laugh, as if to say that the moment for discussing the topic had already passed and that I had asked at the wrong time.

units.source_text: 一见到钱，无论怎样的正人君子都会立刻变成坏人的。”

en.t: Once they see money, even the most upright gentleman immediately becomes a bad person.
